location_qualifier: Taivu / Tasimboko coast, with the Kawaguchi Force
source_locator: R2225: ch. V; R2228: C25080232800 p. 26 (stamp 0464), Kawaguchi landing 29 August–2 September, the 124th Infantry being the core of the force (p. 27, stamp 0465), and HQ and 3rd Battalion landed at Taivu the night of 30 August, destroyer-borne main body at 21:30 on 31 August (p. 36, stamp 0474)
notes: Miller, chapter V: Col. Akinosuka Oka’s 124th Infantry was the nucleus of the Kawaguchi Force, whose echelons arrived 29 August–11 September 1942. Claim date is the first day of that window. Confidence 0.5. Confidence is raised from 0.5 to 0.7. The 17th Army operations record independently confirms the 124th Infantry as the core of Kawaguchi Force and dates HQ and the 3rd Battalion at Taivu on the night of 30 August and the destroyer-borne main body there at 21:30 on 31 August, within the 29 August–2 September landing window that agrees with Miller, chapter V.

location_qualifier: Bloody Ridge, south of Henderson Field
source_locator: R2225: ch. V; R2226: the Edson’s Ridge narrative
current_activity: attacking Bloody Ridge with the Kawaguchi Force
notes: Miller, chapter V, and Zimmerman: the Kawaguchi Force, nucleus the 124th Infantry, attacked Bloody Ridge after nightfall on 13 September 1942. Confidence 0.7.

location_qualifier: west sector of the Lunga defenses, toward the Matanikau
notes: Miller, chapter V: a third Japanese force, probably under Colonel Oka’s command, struck the west sector on the afternoon of 14 September 1942. The hedge “probably” is kept in this note; the claim is entered on the 124th Infantry, Oka’s regiment, at confidence 0.5.

location_qualifier: east of Hill 67, between the Matanikau line and the Lunga perimeter
source_locator: R2225: ch. VI (Oka’s force, seen on 24 October crossing Mount Austen’s foothills, struck the 2nd Battalion, 7th Marines, east of Hill 67 on the night of 25–26 October)
current_activity: attacking the Matanikau–Lunga gap east of Hill 67
notes: Miller, chapter VI: a column reported as commanded by Colonel Oka was seen on 24 October crossing Mount Austen’s foothills; on the night of 25–26 October Oka’s force struck the attenuated line of the 2nd Battalion, 7th Marines, east of Hill 67, broke through at one point, and was driven off. The claim date is 25 October. Confidence 0.5. Hill 67 is not a separate place row; the Matanikau place is used with a qualifier.

source_locator: R2225: ch. X, The Capture of Mount Austen
current_activity: holding the Gifu pillbox line west of the Mount Austen summit with Oka's force
notes: Miller, ch. X: by mid-December 1942 Patch concluded that Japanese troops occupied Mount Austen. He places Oka's force - understrength battalions of the 124th and 228th Infantry, and the 10th Mountain Artillery Regiment - on a 1,500-yard pillbox line west of the summit between Hills 31 and 27 (the Gifu). The 16 December date is the day American patrols had already found fire on the north-west slopes and only abandoned positions on the eastern slopes, and the day Patch ordered the 132nd Infantry to occupy the mountain. Confidence 0.5: Miller only. JACAR vol. 2, as read for the Ke-go withdrawal, does not itself pin the 124th at the Gifu on this day, so the claim is not raised to 0.7.

source_locator: R2225: ch. X, The Capture of Hill 27
current_activity: making six afternoon counterattacks against Hill 27 after its loss
notes: Miller, ch. X: after 2nd Battalion, 132nd Infantry, took Hill 27 on the morning of 2 January 1943, Japanese troops north of the hill - the Gifu garrison Miller had placed as Oka's 124th and 228th - recovered and launched six successive infantry counterattacks that afternoon, supported by mortars, grenade dischargers, machine guns, and some artillery. The 2nd Battalion held the hill. Confidence 0.5: Miller only. The regiment is not separately named in the counterattack paragraph, which refers to "the Japanese north of Hill 27"; the identification is inferred from the mid-December Gifu garrison Miller names, and is annotated as such.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XII, Reduction of the Gifu
current_activity: making a last night attack under Inagaki, then being wiped out in the Gifu
notes: Miller, ch. XII: at 0230 on the night of 22-23 January 1943 about 100 Japanese led by Major Inagaki rushed the sector held by F Company and the Antitank Company, 35th Infantry, and were broken up; 85 dead were counted at daybreak, including Inagaki. On 23 January 2nd Battalion, 35th Infantry, cleared the remnants; the Gifu garrison was almost completely wiped out. The 124th is identified from Miller's earlier placing of Oka's 124th in the Gifu, not from a named 23 January regiment heading, and that inference is annotated. The claim is dated 23 January, the day the position fell. Confidence 0.5: Miller only.
